skill.name: ai-engineer
skill.description: Design production-ready LLM applications, RAG systems, and intelligent agents with safety, observability, evaluation, and cost controls.
skill.summary: Plan and implement reliable LLM, RAG, multimodal, and agent systems for production environments.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives caused by safety and information-retrieval terminology in SKILL.md. The file contains guidance only and does not direct system reconnaissance, jailbreak behavior, code execution, or data exfiltration. No net-new semantic security risks were found.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid sending sensitive data to external models without approval.
- Hybrid search combining vector similarity and keyword matching (BM25)
- "Build a production RAG system for enterprise knowledge base with hybrid search"
- Safety prompting: jailbreak detection, content filtering, bias mitigation

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 explicitly warns against sending sensitive data to external models without approval. This is a protective data-handling rule, not system reconnaissance.
Line 58 describes hybrid document retrieval using vector similarity and BM25. It does not instruct inspection of a host, network, credentials, or environment.
Line 178 is a quoted example request for an enterprise knowledge-base RAG system. Hybrid search here means information retrieval, not reconnaissance.
Line 91 lists jailbreak detection alongside content filtering and bias mitigation as defensive safety prompting. It neither attempts nor instructs a jailbreak.

content.value_statement: Production AI systems require reliable retrieval, orchestration, safety, monitoring, and cost controls. This skill provides structured engineering guidance across the complete LLM application lifecycle.
actual_capabilities: Designs multi-stage RAG pipelines with chunking, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and context filtering.
Recommends models, embedding services, vector databases, and agent frameworks based on cost, latency, reliability, and scale.
Plans production API patterns with streaming, caching, rate limits, fallbacks, and structured outputs.
Designs agent workflows with tools, memory, state management, escalation paths, and evaluation metrics.
Defines safeguards for prompt injection, sensitive data, content moderation, bias, and policy compliance.
Creates testing, monitoring, cost management, and staged rollout strategies for AI services.
limitations: Generated designs and code require environment-specific testing, security review, and operational validation.
The skill does not provide credentials, datasets, infrastructure access, or deployment permissions.
Model and framework recommendations can become outdated as providers change features, pricing, and availability.
Reliable results require clear use cases, data sources, success metrics, constraints, and safety boundaries.

use_cases.title: Add an LLM Feature
use_cases.description: Design a reliable model integration with typed outputs, fallback behavior, testing, and cost limits.

use_cases.title: Build Enterprise RAG
use_cases.description: Plan ingestion, chunking, hybrid retrieval, reranking, evaluation, access control, and production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Define an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn a product workflow into tools, state transitions, guardrails, human escalation, and measurable success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic LLM Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an LLM feature for [use case]. State assumptions, model choice, request flow, safety controls, tests, and a small rollout plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when beginning a focused model-powered product feature.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RAG system for [documents and users]. Cover ingestion, chunking, retrieval, reranking, citations, evaluation, permissions, latency, and cost.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when answers must be grounded in private or domain-specific documents.

prompt_templates.title: Architect an AI Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an agent for [workflow]. Define tools, permissions, state, memory, failure handling, human approval points, observability, and adversarial tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a model must perform several controlled actions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production AI Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture: [details]. Identify reliability, security, quality, latency, and cost risks. Prioritize fixes and define measurable release gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced review before a high-impact production launch.

output_examples.input: Design a RAG system for an internal policy library.
output_examples.output: A staged architecture covering document ingestion, permission-aware hybrid retrieval, reranking, cited answers, offline evaluation, monitoring, and gradual rollout.

output_examples.input: Reduce the cost and latency of an existing support assistant.
output_examples.output: A prioritized plan using model routing, semantic caching, prompt compression, streaming, budget limits, and quality checks before each optimization.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer service agent with refund tools.
output_examples.output: A controlled workflow with scoped tools, explicit approval thresholds, durable state, escalation paths, audit logs, failure recovery, and adversarial tests.

best_practices: Define quality, latency, cost, safety, and reliability targets before selecting models or frameworks.
Evaluate retrieval and generation separately with representative data, adversarial inputs, and traceable failure categories.
Use least-privilege tools, redact sensitive data, require approval for high-impact actions, and monitor production behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not choose an agent when a deterministic workflow or simple model call can solve the task.
Do not send sensitive data to external models without authorization, minimization, redaction, and retention controls.
Do not launch without evaluation baselines, observability, fallback behavior, cost limits, and a rollback plan.

faq.question: What types of systems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers LLM applications, RAG pipelines, AI agents, vector search, multimodal integrations, model APIs, safety controls, and production operations.

faq.question: Does it require a specific model provider?
faq.answer: No. It supports provider-hosted and open-source models, with selection based on quality, latency, cost, privacy, and deployment constraints.

faq.question: Can it design a complete RAG architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It can address ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, context construction, citations, evaluation, permissions, monitoring, and cost.

faq.question: Can it implement autonomous agents?
faq.answer: It can design and implement controlled agent workflows with tools, memory, state, guardrails, evaluation, and human approval points.

faq.question: Does it replace security or compliance review?
faq.answer: No. Its guidance supports engineering decisions, but qualified reviewers must validate privacy, security, legal, and compliance requirements.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the use case, users, data sources, existing stack, constraints, success metrics, permissions, budget, latency targets, and deployment environment.
